name: Portland
tax_rate: 6% city TLT + 2% city tourism tax, plus Multnomah County 5.5% and Oregon state 1.5%; separate 3% Tourism Improvement District fee and $4/night short-term rental fee
deadline_pattern: Travel Portland Visitor Experience Grants open the first week of January and close in early February (Feb. 9, 2026 for the 2026 cycle); decisions by March 31; the 2027 cycle dates had not been posted as of Nov. 4, 2026
annual_pool: Up to $200,000 per cycle for Visitor Experience Grants ($25,000 to $50,000 per award); more than $700,000 awarded to 21 projects since January 2023. Large Event Sponsorships (up to $30,000) and Cultural Enrichment Sponsorships (up to $2,500) run on a separate semiannual calendar
contact: Travel Portland grants team, grants@travelportland.com (no named program officer published); general Travel Portland grants and sponsorships page at travelportland.com/about-us/grants-sponsorships/
notes: The City of Portland does not run its own competitive TLT grant; it contracts Travel Portland, which runs the TLT- and fee-funded Visitor Experience Grant (projects that attract visitors or improve their stay, $25,000 to $50,000, for-profit tourism businesses eligible) plus Large Event Sponsorships for public events of 7,500+ attendees held at least two years with 10%+ out-of-town attendance. A cross-departmental Travel Portland staff committee scores on tourism impact, marketing, equity and accessibility, budget leverage and partnerships; leadership makes final decisions. Organizations may receive one sponsorship per fiscal year and one grant per cycle, and can be funded up to three consecutive years for the same project.
members_source: Visitor Experience Grants are scored by an internal Travel Portland staff committee; no public roster (https://www.travelportland.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2026-Visitor-Experience-Grant-Guidelines.pdf)

presentation.pattern: No applicant presentation; a virtual information session is held the week applications open (Jan. 7, 2026) and grantees do a midway phone or Zoom check-in
presentation.format: Online application and quiz through Travel Portland's grant management platform; no live pitch

meeting_schedule: No public committee meetings; staff review after the February deadline with decisions by March 31. Event sponsorship requests are reviewed twice a year (apply by April 15 for July-December events, by October 15 for January-June events)
pool_note: The $200,000 figure is the Visitor Experience Grant pool only. Portland's roughly $23.9 million in city TLT largely funds Travel Portland's contract, the Portland Expo/convention facilities and the general fund; the amount Travel Portland spends on event sponsorships (up to $30,000 per large event) is not published as a pool.

name: Seaside
tax_rate: 10% city TLT, plus Clatsop County 3% (unincorporated and city-wide county levy) and Oregon state 1.5%
deadline_pattern: Applications open May 1 and are accepted on a rolling basis until the first Friday of December or until funds are exhausted (Dec. 5, 2025 for the 2025-26 cycle; Dec. 4, 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle); the Tourism Advisory Committee reviews at its monthly meeting and notifies within 60 days
typical_open: May 1 (May 1, 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle; May 2, 2025 the year before)
annual_pool: Up to $25,000 for Destination Events and Programming Grants plus up to $25,000 for Community Arts and Vitality Grants each fiscal year; as of September 2026, $22,500 of the events pool was committed with $2,500 remaining and $18,769 of the arts pool committed with $6,231 remaining
contact: Joshua Heineman, Tourism Marketing Director, City of Seaside Visitors Bureau, 503-738-3097, info@seasideor.com (general bureau line; reports are emailed to the tourism director)
notes: The Seaside Visitors Bureau is a city department funded by the 10% room tax, and its Tourism Advisory Committee allocates two small grant pools: Destination Events and Programming ($5,000 standard cap, $7,000 for a new-to-Seaside event in its first year, $3,000 cap for shoulder dates Sept. 8-30 and Mar. 16-May 28, $5,000 cap for Oct. 1-Mar. 15) and Community Arts and Vitality for murals and placemaking. Summer dates (May 29-Sept. 6, 2027) are ineligible; the committee favors proposals that generate commercial lodging room nights in the off-season and requires a detailed financial plan. Because the pool is small and rolling, apply early in the cycle (May) before funds are committed; the 2026-27 events pool was nearly spent by September.

name: Ashland
tax_rate: 10% city transient occupancy tax (state DOR-administered), plus Oregon state 1.5%; no Jackson County tax inside city limits
deadline_pattern: No calendar deadline; Event Partnership Grant applications are accepted first-come, first-served for events occurring before June 30, 2027, due at least 90 days before the event (300+ attendees) or 30 days before (under 300) until the fiscal-year allocation is spent
typical_open: July 1 with each fiscal year (relaunched August 2025 for FY2025-26; FY2026-27 round open as of Nov. 2026)
annual_pool: $150,000 announced for FY2025-26 (Aug. 2025 city release); $100,000 supported 22 events in the first year (Oct. 2024 to mid 2025); FY2026-27 allocation not published
contact: City Manager's Office, 541-552-2103, citymanageroffice@ashlandoregon.gov; Jordan Rooklyn, Deputy City Manager, jordan.rooklyn@ashlandoregon.gov, 541-552-2103
notes: Ashland funds its Event Partnership Grant from the tourism share of its transient occupancy tax and awards it first-come, first-served rather than through a scored committee round: up to $5,000 per event (max $20,000 per series) for events over 300 attendees and up to $2,500 for smaller events, provided the event draws more than 100 people, is publicly advertised and attracts attendees from more than 50 miles away or into overnight lodging. By October 2025 the program had awarded $131,250 across 20 grants covering 25 events (about 6,000 visitors). Apply early in the fiscal year since funds run out; grantees sign an agreement, list the city as sponsor and file a post-event report. Travel Ashland (the chamber) receives the larger marketing contract (about $517,000 in FY2024) but does not run a public grant round.
members_source: No committee; applications are processed by the City Manager's Office on a first-come basis (https://ashlandoregon.gov/EconomicDevelopmentGrants)

presentation.pattern: No presentation; online form reviewed by staff
presentation.format: Online application form (FormCenter) with grant agreement on award

meeting_schedule: None; staff administered. Ashland City Council meets the first and third Tuesdays and sets the annual tourism allocation in the biennial budget
pool_note: The $150,000 is the FY2025-26 Event Partnership Grant allocation, fully open to outside applicants. Ashland's roughly $3 million TOT is split 30.96% tourism and 69.04% general fund under its pre-2003 grandfathering; the tourism share also pays Travel Ashland's marketing contract and beautification grants (FY2024 tourism grants totaled about $833,000 including $517,000 to Travel Ashland).

name: Hood River
tax_rate: 8% city transient room tax, plus Oregon state 1.5% (Hood River County levies its own tax only in unincorporated areas)
deadline_pattern: Visit Hood River's Community Investment Matching Grant opens in mid-March and closes April 30 at 5 p.m. (March 16 to April 30, 2026 for the 2026-27 program); the 2027 dates had not been posted as of Nov. 4, 2026
annual_pool: Up to $40,000 in matching funds in 2026 (six awards of $4,000 to $10,000), up from about $27,000 in 2025 and $27,600 in 2023; more than $140,000 to 21 recipients since the program began in 2022
contact: Katie Kadlub, CEO, Visit Hood River (Hood River County Chamber of Commerce), 800-366-3530; application and guidelines posted at visithoodriver.com each March in English and Spanish
notes: The City of Hood River has no grant program of its own; its roughly $1.6 million to $2.0 million in room tax goes to the general fund and a tourism promotion contract. The chamber-run DMO, Visit Hood River, operates the annual Community Investment Matching Grant, which it describes as reinvesting tourism dollars from the public and private funds it manages; the funding is treated here as the local tourism grant but Visit Hood River has not stated the TRT share. Awards favor new events, programs and trail or placemaking projects with a matching contribution, and businesses have been funded (Pear Bloom Farm, Hood River Hotel, Button Bridge Comedy Jamboree). Each project needs its own application.

name: Beaverton
tax_rate: 4% city TLT, plus Washington County 9% and Oregon state 1.5%
deadline_pattern: Explore Tualatin Valley's Inspiration Event Award takes applications July 1 to Sept. 30 (awards by Oct. 31, for November-May events) and Feb. 1 to April 30 (awards by May 31, for June-October events); the Strategic Investment Grant takes applications July 1 to Sept. 15 with awards by Dec. 15; the FY2027 guideline dates had not been confirmed as of Nov. 4, 2026
typical_open: July 1 and Feb. 1 (event awards); July 1 (strategic investment grants)
annual_pool: Pool not published; the October 2025 Inspiration round distributed $16,500 across ten Washington County events (up to $5,000 each); Strategic Investment Grants are up to $20,000 with a 25% applicant match
contact: Explore Tualatin Valley, engage@tualatinvalley.org; Dave Parulo, President and CEO; Sylke Neal-Finnegan, Vice President of Marketing and Communications
notes: The City of Beaverton has no TLT grant program; its 4% city tax goes to the general fund. Tourism grants in Beaverton come through Explore Tualatin Valley (formerly Washington County Visitors Association), the county DMO funded by 2.33% of the 9% Washington County TLT, which runs the semiannual Inspiration Event Award (up to $5,000 for public, visitor-facing events; one per organization per fiscal year) and the annual Strategic Investment Grant (up to $20,000, 75% ETV share). Both are limited to Washington County 501(c) nonprofits, tribes and government partners, so a for-profit producer needs a nonprofit or city co-applicant; the Beaverton Downtown Association received a 2025 award for Booverton. Priority goes to multi-day, off-season events that generate paid overnight stays.

name: Pendleton
tax_rate: 8% city transient room tax plus a $1.50 per room-night ($0.50 per RV space) Travel Promotion Assessment; Oregon state 1.5%; no Umatilla County tax inside city limits
deadline_pattern: Travel Pendleton Marketing Grant applications are due by the last day of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, Sept. 30, Dec. 31) and reviewed monthly within the quarter; awards depend on event date and application volume
typical_open: Continuous; submit any time before the quarter's end
annual_pool: Not published; maximum $3,000 per award, reimbursed against invoices and spent within one year
contact: Kara Woolsey, Travel Pendleton (Pendleton Chamber of Commerce), director@travelpendleton.com, 541-276-7411, 501 S Main St, Pendleton, OR 97801
notes: Pendleton's 8% room tax is split 14% to the chamber for marketing, 48% to the convention center, 35% general fund and 1.75% public art; the chamber's Travel Pendleton Committee also receives 60% of the separate per-night Travel Promotion Assessment and uses it for the quarterly Marketing Grant (up to $3,000, for-profit and nonprofit organizers eligible) and a Room Rebate Program for groups. Grants must fund marketing that reaches residents at least 100 miles away, organizers must stay in city-limits lodging during the event, and scoring favors a lodging partner, shoulder-season dates (April to mid-June, August, mid-September to March), projected room nights and new or expanded events. A wrap-up report with room-night counts is due within 45 days.
members_source: Travel Pendleton Committee (Pendleton Chamber of Commerce); member roster not published online

presentation.pattern: No presentation; written application reviewed monthly by the Travel Pendleton Committee
presentation.format: PDF application emailed or mailed to the chamber

meeting_schedule: Travel Pendleton Committee reviews applications monthly; dates not published
pool_note: City TRT is about $964,000 (2009 projection was $785,000 TRT plus $200,000 TPA); the chamber's 14% TRT share would be roughly $135,000 plus 60% of the TPA, but Travel Pendleton does not publish how much of that is set aside for grants versus its own marketing.

tax_rate: City transient room tax budgeted as 7% to the general fund, 1% to public safety and 4% to tourism (marketing and facilities), which implies a 12% city rate; the starting list showed 8%. Plus Oregon state 1.5%
annual_pool: No grant pool. FY2026-27 budget: $2,100,000 in room tax of which $350,000 is tourism marketing/promotion and $350,000 tourism-related facilities; only $120,000 is budgeted for marketing spending and $38,175 for facility supplies, with the rest held in a $2.9 million unappropriated balance and $187,350 tourism infrastructure reserve
contact: Kimberly Wollenburg, City Administrator/Recorder, info@cityofdepoebay.org, City Hall, 570 SE Shell Avenue, Depoe Bay, OR 97341 (RFP 2025-02 contact; phone not published)
notes: Depoe Bay collects about $2.1 million a year in room tax but runs no grant program. The FY2026-27 budget (Resolution 609-26) routes $1,225,000 to the general fund, $565,000 to sheriff and fire contracts, $200,000 to the Harbor Fund, $325,000 to ADA restrooms at Harbor View and only $120,000 to tourism marketing, with a $2.9 million unappropriated balance in the Transient Room Tax Fund. The city issued RFP 2025-02 in January 2025 to hire a destination management organization (proposals due Feb. 27, 2025; the RFP is now closed and no award has been posted). There is no tourism committee; requests would go to the city administrator and council. Depoe Bay is a prime example of unspent tourism-restricted TLT.

tax_rate: 5% county TLT in unincorporated areas (a November 2018 measure to add 3% for the fairgrounds and sheriff was referred by commissioners), plus Oregon state 1.5%; Enterprise 5% and Joseph 3% levy their own city taxes
annual_pool: Not published; Commissioner Todd Nash cited about $360,000 in county lodging tax collections in 2018. Small TLT grants (for example $1,000 to the Courthouse Concert Series in 2026) are approved by the Board of Commissioners on request

name: Hines
tax_rate: 8% city TLT, plus Oregon state 1.5%; Harney County has discussed a county TLT (2026)
annual_pool: City staff estimated $62,500 of TRT had to go to tourism in FY2019-20 (25% share), of which $53,000 was planned for the Harney County Chamber and $9,500 left for council direction; since Ordinance 327 the council sets the tourism allocation each budget year
contact: City of Hines, City Administrator, 101 E Barnes Ave, Hines, OR 97738 (Kirby Letham held the role in 2019); Harney County Chamber of Commerce, 484 N Broadway, Burns, 541-573-2636, director@harneycounty.com
notes: Hines reserves 25% of its TRT for tourism. In June 2019 councilors objected to sending the full share (about $53,000 of an estimated $62,500) to the Harney County Chamber without evidence of benefit to Hines events such as Obsidian Days, and Ordinance 327 (July 9, 2019) repealed the automatic chamber payment so the council now decides the tourism allocation annually, with the mayor suggesting a fixed chamber percentage set at budget time. No application form, committee or award list has been published since; treat it as an ad hoc request to the city administrator before spring budget hearings. Harney County Judge Bill Hart discussed a county-level TLT in April 2026.

tax_rate: 10% county TLT in unincorporated areas (raised from 7% by Ordinance 25-01, effective July 1, 2025), plus Oregon state 1.5%
deadline_pattern: Not yet published. At the May 13, 2026 budget committee meeting staff said a competitive grant program for tourism, facade improvements and marketing was being drafted with 'guardrails' for allocation, with most new revenue not expected until FY2027
annual_pool: Not published; the board chair said the TLT increase and a legislative shift to a 50/50 split could add close to $600,000 in unrestricted funds, part of which is being considered for the competitive grant program; most would not arrive until FY2027
contact: Miranda Plagge, Economic Development Administrator, Curry County Economic Development Department, 541-247-3222, econdev@currycountyor.gov
notes: Curry County raised its unincorporated-area lodging tax from 7% to 10% under Ordinance 25-01 (effective July 1, 2025) to seed 'Curry's Destination Development Fund' under the county Economic Development Department's 2022 Destination Strategy, with infrastructure grants (trails, signage, visitor amenities) and advertising support for tourism-related businesses. No application, deadline, pool or scoring document has been published; email econdev@currycountyor.gov to get on the notification list. Incorporated cities (Brookings, Gold Beach, Port Orford) levy their own TLT.
